title: Cardinals' Grueling 11-Game Trip Featured Historical Highs, Languishing Lows, Awful End
description: With the Cardinals wrapping up their longest road trip of the season -- three cities, 11 games and 10 days -- here is a look back at history made by Joshua Báez in Chicago, a near collapse in Cincinnati, two starter injuries and a stomach-turning finish in Philadelphia.
fullText:
Roundtable Sports' John Denton breaks down the Cardinals' epic ninth-inning collapse on Sunday that allowed the Phillies to score six straight runs after two were out for the win.

The Cardinals' longest, most grueling road trip of theseason is finally behind them, and assuredly not a second too soon in theireyes considering the toll it took on the short-handed squad over the past 10days.

What had the makings of a 6-5 trip that kept the Cardinalsin the chase for a Wild Card slot devolved into a forgettable 5-6 trip in aconfounding stretch of five batters on Sunday in Philadelphia. Up 4-0 with twoouts in the ninth, the Cardinals had a 99.6% percent chance to lock up afeel-good victory before flying back to St. Louis for a much-needed day off. Ashit by hit piled up, culminating in Kyle Schwarber's 459-foot blast over thebatter's eye in center field, and the Cards were left looking for answersfollowing a 6-4 loss and a collapse of epic proportions.

ABSOLUTE CINEMA. pic.twitter.com/g1T1SpeTdB

And it wasn't even the moment with the most historicsignificance on a trip filled with incredible highs and devastating lows. Hereis a look back at the three-city, 11-game, 10-day road trip that was for theCards.

Friday, Aug. 14 (Cubs 3, Cards 0):Matthew Liberatore was perfect for 4 1/3 innings and took a shutout into thesixth inning before encountering trouble and giving way to reliever GeorgeSoriano. The reliever's fourth pitch was hit in the left field bleachers atWrigley Field by Seiya Suzuki for a three-run homer.

Saturday, Aug. 15 (Cards 8, Cubs 4): In thefirst game of his big-league career, Joshua Báez put on a show in the greatestMLB debut in the history of the game. Báez drilled the first pitch he saw 449feet for a homer that nearly went out of Wrigley Field. In his second at bat,he worked the count from 0-2 to 3-2 and hit a line-drive laser into theleft-field bleachers for a solo shot. That made him just the third player inhistory to homer in his first two at bats.

3 home runs in his first 3 Major League at-bats 😤

Did Joshua Báez put on the best MLB debut EVER?! pic.twitter.com/P43Qi4d4cn

Two innings later, Báez did the unthinkable by going with aslider on the outside corner and driving it over the wall in right-center for athird homer in three MLB at bats. The 6-foot-3, 220-pound slugger had a shot atfourth straight homer in the seventh inning, but he lined out to left field –something that drew a raucous ovation from the Wrigley Field faithful.

Sunday, Aug. 16 (Cards 11, Cubs 4): AlecBurleson (homer run, four RBI) and Jordan Walker (home run, four RBI) did allthe heavy lifting in this romp.

Báez's encore: 0 for 5 with three strikeouts.

Monday, Aug. 17 (Game 1 – Cards 2, Reds 1):Burleson drove in two in the first inning and rookie Quinn Mathews and fiverelievers made it stand up.

Monday, Aug. 17 (Game 2 – Reds 6, Reds 5): AndrePallante, a 12-game winner on the season, allowed a season-most 10 hits and waspulled after 88 pitches and with a three-run lead. (Put a pin in this one).

Ivan Herrera threw out his first base runner after allowing60 straight stolen bases … and it was Elly De La Cruz.

The vibes are HIGH for the #STLCards.

Ivan Herrera throws out Elly De La Cruz, his first caught stealing since 2024. Then immediately after, ties the game with a solo homer!pic.twitter.com/DeOlP8vcLK

Peter Strzelecki bailed out a tired bullpen with threestrong innings, but he surrendered a game-tying solo homer to Dane Myers withtwo outs in the bottom of the ninth inning. De La Cruz won it with a walk-offhit in the 10th inning.

Tuesday, Aug. 18 (Cards 3, Reds 0): KyleLeahy shut out the Reds over five innings – his 10th straight startof allowing two earned runs or fewer. Shortstop Masyn Winn homered and doubledtwice for the first three-extra-base game of his career.

Wednesday, Aug. 19 (Reds 5, Cardinals 4):Liberatore struck out nine in six innings while protecting a 2-0 lead. However,he grooved a 1-2 pitch that Sal Stewart hit 422 feet for a go-ahead, three-runhomer.

Thursday, Aug. 20 (Cards 10, Reds 9): In awild game that would have perfectly encapsulated this trip if not for Sunday'sstunner, the Cards led 4-0, trailed 5-4, led 10-5 and won 10-9 in an exhaustingback-and-forth.

Reliever Ryne Stanek surrendered a grand slam to MattMcLain, but he was let off the hook when Myers dropped what should have been agame-ending fly ball in the top of the ninth inning. The Cards scored six timesto take a seemingly safe five-run lead into the bottom of the ninth.

DANE MYERS DROPS THE FINAL OUT AND THE CARDINALS LEAD pic.twitter.com/QwHkpZ8L8B

However, Soriano (three walks) and All-Star closer Riley O'Brien(two walks) were wild and pitching on fumes. The game ended only after Walkerran down McLain's drive to the warning track with the tying and go-ahead runs inscoring position.

Friday, Aug. 21 (Phillies 7, Cards 6, 10innings): The day started in ominous fashion when Pallante continuedto experience pain during a bullpen session and was placed on the 15-dayInjured List with right elbow inflammation. He was the first Cards starting pitcherto go on the IL in 23 months, dating to September of 2024.

Things got worse when Hunter Dobbins had to leave after onepitch of the fifth inning with right forearm tightness – an injury that also landedhim on the Injured List.

As for the game, it was the best-played game of the tripand it had a playoff-like atmosphere. Báez and Walker smashed two-run homers.

BOHM SENDS US HOME! pic.twitter.com/ec9jBqKEga

A key moment came when Cards centerfielder Everson Pereirawas hit on the back of the hand and had to leave the game in the eighth. Philliesfirst baseman Alec Bohm drilled a shot to the deepest part of the park in the10th, and when utility fielder Jose Fermin – filling in for theinjured Pereira – couldn't haul it in, it went down as a game-winning, two-runtriple.

Saturday, Aug. 22 (Phillies 12, Cards 3): Thesurging Phillies overwhelmed Mathews with three runs in the first and four morein the third inning. The night ended with reserve catcher Pedro Pages on themound.

Sunday, Aug. 23 (Phillies 6, Cards 4): St.Louis dominated every aspect of the game for 8 2/3 innings and looked poised toavoid a sweep with their finest win. Burleson drove in two, Jose Fermin homeredand JJ Wetherholt had an RBI single against Phillies ace Cristopher Sanchez,who came into the day 11-1 at home this season. Leahy was strong again, but hewas pulled after four innings and 63 pitches.

Ferminator sends it out! pic.twitter.com/kYanEsWMXR

The bullpen held strong until O'Brien's collapse aftergetting two outs in the ninth. He got to within a strike of the win threetimes, but JT Realmuto singled, Edmundo Sosa doubled in three runs on a balldown the third base line that shouldn't have gotten by rookie Blaze Jordan andwhen No. 9 hitter Bryan De La Cruz drilled a spinning sweeper for a single thatknotted the game. Despite seeing what had happened three days earlier inCincinnati with O'Brien, Cardinals' manager Oliver Marmol stuck with hiscloser. Schwarber hit O'Brien's 39th pitch a staggering 459 feet forhis 39th homer of the season.

title: Former Penn State 1,000-Yard WR Labeled as NFL's Most Overpaid WR
description: Penn State has sent plenty of good players to the NFL over the years, with Saquon Barkley being one of the best. He earned a huge payday from the Philadelphia Eagles and is well worth his huge extension.
fullText:
Penn State has sent plenty of good players to the NFL over the years, with Saquon Barkley being one of the best. He earned a huge payday from the Philadelphia Eagles and is well worth his huge extension.

But not all of the former Nittany Lions players in the NFL are worth as much as they are getting paid right now. Some are earning more than they maybe should, considering their talents.

In Garrett Podell of CBS Sports' opinion, one former Penn State wide receiver, who had over 1,000 yards in one season with the Nittany Lions, is the most overpaid WR in the NFL. That WR is Tampa Bay Buccaneers veteran Chris Godwin.

"Chris Godwin's three-year, $66 million extension is aging like spoiled milk," Podell writes. "He has missed a combined 18 games over the last two seasons, eight of which came in 2025, when he registered career lows in catches (33) and receiving yards (360) while producing the second-fewest receiving touchdowns of his career (two)."

Godwin is a 30-year-old wide receiver who was drafted in the third round, at 84th overall, by the Buccaneers back in 2017.

He's since won a Super Bowl, catching passes from Tom Brady, and was named a Pro Bowler back in 2019 when he had 1,333 receiving yards.

In his NFL career, Godwin has 612 receptions on 867 targets for 7,626 yards and 41 touchdowns. He's also one first-down shy of 400 for his NFL career.

Godwin is one of the best WRs to come out of Penn State in school history, but now, at 30 years old entering his 10th season in the league, he's considered the most overpaid WR in the league.

Spending $22 million per-year on Godwin is a bit too much, considering he just had back-to-back seasons playing under 10 games and recording under 600 receiving yards.

During his time at Penn State, only his freshman season, when he caught 26 passes for 338 yards and two TDs, was worse. He had 1,101 yards and five TDS in 2015, and 982 yards and 11 TDs in 2016.

While Godwin could bounce back in 2026 for the Buccaneers, the former Penn State star WR is currently overpaid and is arguably the most overpaid WR in the NFL.

But even if he doesn't do a whole lot more for the rest of his NFL career, it's still been a massive success for the Nittany Lions WR in the NFL, as he's been arguably the best WR Penn State has ever sent to the league.

title: Bills injury update: Keon Coleman in walking boot, latest on 12 players
description: Keon Coleman remains in a walking boot. Here's the latest on Khalil Shakir, Ed Oliver and other injured Bills entering the final preseason week.
fullText:
Keon Coleman is still wearing a walking boot.

The Buffalo Bills wide receiver was one of 28 players who didn't play in Saturday's 31-7 preseason victory over the Cleveland Browns, though many of those absences had nothing to do with injuries.

Josh Allen, James Cook, D.J. Moore and most starters were held out after getting extensive work during Thursday's joint practice.

But Coleman, Khalil Shakir and Ed Oliver were among the Bills sidelined by injuries, while rookie offensive lineman Jude Bowry went into the medical tent during Saturday's game.

Here's the latest on Buffalo's injuries heading into the final week of the preseason.

Coleman did not play against the Browns and remained in a walking boot before the game.

NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported Thursday that Coleman is dealing with a foot/toe injury.

Coleman played in Buffalo's preseason opener against Carolina, catching three passes for 17 yards, including a 9-yard touchdown from Allen.

Bills coach Joe Brady indicated after the game that there wasn't concern about Coleman, but the receiver did not participate in Thursday's joint practice with Cleveland.

Shakir also missed the joint practice and did not play against Cleveland.

Brady confirmed Thursday that Shakir's absence was injury-related but did not provide specifics.

Shakir was on the field before Saturday's game working with athletic trainers while wearing a sleeve on his right leg.

Oliver did not travel to Cleveland for the joint practice or preseason game.

Brady confirmed after Saturday's game that Oliver's absence was injury-related.

Oliver played in the preseason opener against Carolina but did not practice last week.

Oliver and his family are also grieving the death of his young son, which the Bills publicly acknowledged Saturday before the game.

The Bills added at least one injury concern during Saturday's game.

Bowry went into the medical tent and was replaced at right tackle by Chase Lundt. Bowry returned to the sideline but spent the Bills' next offensive series on the bench.

Brady did not provide an update on Bowry's injury after the game.

Bell missed his second consecutive preseason game because of a hamstring injury.

Bell suffered the injury during the Return of the Blue & Red practice Aug. 8 at new Highmark Stadium and hasn't played in either of Buffalo's first two preseason games.

Johnson remains sidelined after suffering a lower-body injury during the Return of the Blue & Red practice.

Johnson was going one-on-one with linebacker Joe Andreessen when he went down near the right sideline and grabbed his right leg. A trainer helped Johnson walk off the field.

Johnson hasn't played in either preseason game. He was on the field before Saturday's game wearing a sleeve on his right leg.

McGovern also hasn't played this preseason after suffering a lower-body injury during the Return of the Blue & Red practice.

McGovern grabbed the back of his right leg while trying to chase down Christian Benford following an interception. He walked off the field with trainers.

McGovern was on the field before Saturday's game working with athletic trainers but did not play.

Gardner-Johnson has yet to play this preseason.

Gardner-Johnson was carted off the practice field Aug. 1 but returned to practice five days later.

He left practice early Aug. 10 and has remained sidelined from preseason games.

Hairston missed his second consecutive preseason game with a lower-body injury.

Hairston initially sat out the final training camp practice at St. John Fisher University on Aug. 7. The Bills indicated at the time they weren't concerned about his long-term availability.

He dressed and warmed up before the preseason opener against Carolina but didn't play.

Cole Bishop did not play against the Browns after missing the preseason opener with a lower-body injury.

Bishop suffered the injury during the Return of the Blue & Red practice Aug. 8 and missed practice time the following week.

Bishop returned to practice Aug. 18 and participated in Thursday's joint practice against Cleveland.

Shavers remains on the physically unable to perform list while recovering from the torn ACL he suffered during last season's playoffs.

The receiver has not participated in training camp or the preseason.

Hoecht continues to work his way back from the torn right Achilles he suffered last season.

The veteran edge rusher has participated in training camp but hasn't played in either preseason game.

He is expected to play in the third preseason game.

"He's going to hit the field before the regular season starts," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said last week. "He's in a great spot."

title: Former Washington Football DT Cashes in on New Buccaneers Contract
description: After a brief hold-in former Washington Huskies defensive lineman Vita Vea has cashed in on his recent success with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
fullText:
Former Washington Huskies defensive lineman Vita Vea is staying with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after agreeing to a new deal on Thursday.

Vea, a first-round pick (12th overall) by the Buccaneers in the 2018 NFL draft, had been observing practice from the sidelines over the past few weeks while working out a restructured contract. According to multiple reports, the two-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl LV champion has signed a one-year, $30 million extension to remain with the NFC South franchise.

Earlier this month, Vea's camp requested a trade for the two-time All-Pac-12 selection at UW, with it appearing at the time that the two sides wouldn't be able to come to an agreement. Instead, before the Buccaneers' second preseason game ahead of the 2026 NFL regular season, the two sides found mutual ground to reward the standout interior defensive lineman for the next two years.

Bucs have reached an agreement on a one year, $30 million contract with Vita Vea.

This season, Vea will now earn $24 million, a $6 million raise from his previous base salary of $18 million, with $24 million coming to the California native in 2027 to total $30 million in new money.

"Vita is exactly the type of player and person we want to build around in Tampa Bay," general manager Jason Licht said in a press release.

"He has been a dominant force in the middle of our defense, an exceptional teammate, and a tremendous leader in our locker room. One of the keys to our recent success has been our ability to draft, develop, and re-sign core, foundational players who set the standard for what it means to be a Buccaneer. As one of our team leaders, Vita has played a big role in establishing that winning culture, and we are excited to have him continuing to help lead the way as we pursue our next championship."

Vea has made 78 starts over the past five seasons for the Buccaneers with 183 total tackles, 37 tackles for loss and 27.5 sacks, proving to be one of the best nose tackles in the National Football League.

The former UW star ranks eighth in franchise history and has recorded the most sacks of any nose tackle in the NFL since 2019, a key reason why the Buccaneers and one of the league's best interior defensive linemen made sure to stay together for the next two seasons.

title: Why does college football generate so many Freezing Cold Takes?
description: Fred Segal is no different than a lot of fans. When he was an attorney, he would consume sports takes just like anyone else: scrolling Twitter, watching ESPN, and listening to the radio. Mostly, he accepted the bold opinions and predictions for what they were — entertainment. But there was one thing that always got…
fullText:
Fred Segal is no different than a lot of fans. When he was an attorney, he would consume sports takes just like anyone else: scrolling Twitter, watching ESPN, and listening to the radio.

Mostly, he accepted the bold opinions and predictions for what they were — entertainment. But there was one thing that always got under Fred's skin. He hated watching or listening to these pundits pat themselves on the back when one of their bold takes came to fruition.

"I'd see a reporter make a prediction about a team and that team lost, and I'd be like, 'oh, that guy was wrong,'" he told Awful Announcing in an interview. "Then he'd say the same thing the next week about another team, and that team lost, or he'd say something about a player that was going to be great, and then they weren't.

"I'd remember those and then later on that same guy would say something like, 'just like I predicted five days ago, this happened,' and I'd be like, 'Hang on! I can remember three off the top of my head where you were dead wrong. You didn't post those!'"

That is how Freezing Cold Takes was born, and it didn't take long for it to become one of the Twitter feeds every sports fan had to follow.

"I started doing it for fun," Segal said. "Just a troll type thing, maybe."

Those followers wanted to do so much of Segal's research for him, and that troll grew into a real business. Last week, Segal released his second book. Freezing Cold Takes: College Football catalogs plenty of nonsensical opinions and plenty of predictions that turned out to be very, very wrong.

Writing the book was a business opportunity, but it also gave Segal a chance to put some of the best misfires down on paper. That's pretty valuable when your brand was built on the unstable foundations of social media. Plus, it was easy, a pleasure even, for Segal.

Research for the book combined two of his favorite things: reading old newspaper articles and talking about college football. Segal keeps an eye on all sports takes, but as an SEC alum, his radar is always up for college football. It's his favorite sport, and it's the sport that might most consistently give him material.

"The emotion and the passion, nothing beats it," he says. "Everybody takes it so personally. Even in terms of the writers and TV personalities, every game creates a narrative about who is going to the playoff or what coach has to be fired after his second loss."

I asked Segal if he knew who was featured the most in Freezing Cold Takes: College Football. He didn't have the official stats handy, but his guess was either former CBS and Bleacher Report writer Barrett Sallee, OutKick founder Clay Travis, or Yahoo's Dan Wolken.

To be fair to them, though, in 2022, Segal told Dan Patrick that he had to stop tracking Skip Bayless's and Colin Cowherd's missed predictions because they were dominating the Freezing Cold Takes Twitter feed. Had he not made that decision, he may have been able to fill a whole book with just misfires from those two men.

Social media is a tricky thing now. Gauging what value your idea would have in a different environment is hard too. Maybe that's why Segal is quick to point out that he probably would have been beaten to the punch when I ask how he thinks Freezing Cold Takes would have fared if he had launched in 2025 instead of 2015.

He does note that maybe niche content isn't as valuable on social media as it used to be.

"Some very basic concepts on Twitter now work. I'll see something and think, 'oh, this is pretty basic,' and then it just blows up. I can't even tell anymore what people like and what they don't with social media."

People that have been in the sports talk game for a long time know Segal's work. Even if some privately hate it, in public, everyone will say that they know it's all in good fun. They may even say they welcome the occasional heat check.

In my years writing about sports media, though, I have had the chance to talk to students in high schools and universities across the South, and I've been shocked by what a lot of them have to say about Freezing Cold Takes.

So many people in the very early days of their careers view being highlighted by Segal's social media channels as a credibility killer. That was never what Segal intended.

"I don't think it really diminishes credibility. If anything, I think that credibility is already diminished the second a fan reads something they don't like," he says, pointing out how easy it is now for fans to find the exact opinion about their team that they want to read and believe.

Hot takes are a vital part of this industry. Sports talk is the entertainment business, after all. The stakes of what Wolken, Travis, Sallee, Cowherd, and Bayless think will happen just aren't that high. Isn't being interesting what matters most? Being right should just be a bonus.

"The ones who take [Freezing Cold Takes] seriously, I've come to realize they believe that they are doing work that's important," Segal says. "Whether it's covering a team or breaking stories, they are doing important stuff, and they work long and hard to do it. Then I come along, pass around one bad thing, and everyone laughs about it."

Segal has built a thriving business for himself, but there's no mission to the work. The community he has created is there for comedy purposes just as much as sports ones. Are you worried about seeing your name or take show up in his Twitter feed? Then you are, to borrow a phrase, hustling backward.

"It doesn't matter, right? Like, nobody's ever been fired for bad predictions ever. I mean, I can't even think of one."

title: Premier League forward’s agent ‘working hard’ to find new club before deadline with Man United approached
description: Jean-Philippe Mateta’s agents are said to be ‘working hard’ to find him a new club amid growing uncertainty over his Crystal Palace future.According to TeamTalk, Manchester United and Tottenham ...
fullText:
Jean-Philippe Mateta's agents are said to be 'working hard' to find him a new club amid growing uncertainty over his Crystal Palace future.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur have been contacted to gauge whether they'd be interested in signing the frontman.

His situation at Selhurst Park has turned sour this year, particularly since his proposed £26 million transfer to AC Milan collapsed in the winter window after issues were flagged in his medical regarding a previous meniscus injury.

Although he returned to action for the Eagles and went on to play a key role in their UEFA Conference League triumph, Mateta has still been planning a move elsewhere, despite Palace having no desire to sell him.

He has now raised concerns over their handling of his contract and the validity of the 12-month option triggered by Palace, keeping him tied to the club until June 2027.

Regardless of the outcome of the 29-year-old's dispute, he is keen to seal an agreement with a new club before the September 1 deadline.

United have previously been linked with Mateta, but they have never materialised their interest by submitting a formal bid.

It's thought that INEOS are in the market for a new centre-forward to ease the goalscoring burden on Benjamin Sesko, and while the Palace talisman is slightly older than the players they would usually target, he does now boast six seasons' worth of Premier League experience.

Despite being embroiled in controversy with Palace's board, manager Pierre Sage did opt to start Mateta for the side's season-opener against Everton on Saturday.

He played for just over an hour at the Hill Dickinson Stadium but was unable to make an impact as Palace slumped to a 2-0 defeat.

title: Michigan State football 2026 game-by-game predictions: Oregon
description: Predicting every Michigan State football game for the 2026 season -- next up is a home conference game against the Oregon Ducks
fullText:
Michigan State football is right around the corner so it's time to start predicting how the season will shake out for the Spartans.

Michigan State football is under new leadership this season, with Pat Fitzgerald set to take over as the next head coach. He will take over a program looking to get back on the winning side, with the Spartans in the midst of a four-year bowl drought. Can he get the job done and get the Spartans back to a bowl game this season? I have offered my thoughts on that in our game-by-game predictions segment on Spartans Wire.

We continue on with the next of my game-by-game predictions for each of the matchups on the Spartans' 2026 schedule. Each morning a new prediction will be released following Michigan State's schedule. Next up is a Big Ten matchup against Oregon…

Location: Spartan Stadium (East Lansing, Mich.)

Oregon starting quarterback and preseason Heisman candidate Dante Moore is from Detroit, and was once considering Michigan State for his collegiate career. Moore was a five-star prospect in the 2023 class, and Michigan State was very much involved at one point in his recruitment. He ultimately ended up at UCLA out of high school and later transferred to Oregon where he has experienced a successful college career.

MSU predicted record: 6-4 (4-3 in Big Ten)

Michigan State comes into this Friday night senior day matchup off the high of clinching a bowl berth the week prior. The Spartans upset the Huskies in their previous game to clinch a bowl berth for the first time since 2021.

At the worst, Oregon is 8-2 coming into this game but very well could be undefeated. Either way, they'll be firmly in the mix for a spot in the College Football Playoff and highly motivated to leave East Lansing with a victory.

This is a bad matchup for the Spartans, and I fear depth this late in the season will be catching up with them against a national championship contending team like the Oregon Ducks. I have a hard time finding a path for Michigan State to keep this game terribly close and predict this one to be hand for the Ducks most of the way.

Next on the game-by-game predictions list is a road Big Ten game vs. Rutgers. That prediction will be released tomorrow.

title: WNBA in Vancouver: Isabelle Harrison leads Toronto in rebounds
description: Isabelle Harrison leads Toronto in rebounds against Las Vegas in Vancouver.
fullText:
Las Vegas (26-13) defeated Toronto (11-26), 88-78, on Sunday at Rogers Arena in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. 15,877 were in attendance for the WNBA game.

title: LSU transfer Ashton Stamps ready to leave his mark on ASU football
description: Ashton Stamps was a starter at LSU in 2024 but didn't play much in 2025. He came to the Arizona State football program looking for a new opportunity.
fullText:
Keith Abney declared for the NFL draft. Javan Robinson entered the transfer portal. And just like that, ASU's two most experienced cornerbacks were gone.

The Sun Devils were in the market for quality help at that position. Ashton Stamps was in the transfer portal, and the move made sense for both parties.

"I was looking for a home where I can come and not 'be comfortable,' but be comfortable in the space that I am," Stamps said after practice wrapped up in late August. "Being able to be myself and at the same time have a family to have fun with."

Growing up in Harvey, Louisiana, outside of New Orleans, Stamps quickly became an LSU fan. It was indeed his dream school. Coming out of Archbishop Rummel High, he had offers from schools, including Nebraska and Missouri, but he wanted to stay close to home.

He made a splash during his freshman season, which isn't always easy in the SEC. He played in 11 games in 2023, including four starts, with injuries to athletes higher on the depth chart paving the way for opportunity.

He maintained that momentum, starting all 13 games at cornerback as a sophomore in 2024, and he was among the leaders for passes defended in the SEC

Stamps then found out a player can drop on the depth chart as fast as rise.

In 2025, the Tigers brought in Mansoor Delane, a transfer from Virginia Tech, who went on to be drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs. LSU also had a rapidly improving underclassman in P.J. Woodland and five-star prospect DJ Pickett.

Three games into the 2025 season, Stamps opted to leave the program to retain his redshirt.

"Sometimes you have to be able to block out the noise," he said. "People have their opinions. People are going to say what they're going to say. The difference between the SEC and here is the fan bases and how they take things. It's a mental thing.

"At the end of the day, football is football. You hone in on it, details on and off the football field, it all works out."

ASU assistant coach Bryan Carrington reached out to Stamps right away. The player also traveled to North Carolina and heard a pitch from Bill Belichick, but when he visited Tempe, he committed right away.

"Ashton's a guy who really loves football," Carrington said. "Stuff happens in college football. A lot of guys get lost. I say it all the time, talent is everywhere; opportunity isn't. Ashton's here for the opportunity that Keith vacated, and the plan for him is to follow in those footsteps.

"He has 12 opportunities to achieve all of his dreams, and I feel like he'll get that. He's getting poured in, and he doesn't have to look over his shoulder. Right now, he's in the lane he envisioned himself when he went to college. I'm happy that we were able to provide that lane."

What struck Stamps most about head coach Kenny Dillingham and the staff was authenticity.

"They tell you like it is, not what they think you want to hear. Everything was real," he said. "It felt like everything was lining up. I also wanted the opportunity to go away from home, be able to learn away from my family and grow."

Stamps was one of the team's top performers in fall camp and looks to have locked down one of the corner positions, with junior Rodney Bimage, who saw time in a reserve role last season, likely at the other. Going against the wide receivers in receivers coach Hines Ward's room has been good.

Carrington is excited about the pairing he has now.

"I feel like camp is over, but our standards aren't, and I feel like those guys have tunnel vision for the season," Carrington said. "You can have a good football camp, but when the season starts flying, that's what really matters.

"Stamps, who brings a wealth of experience, is excited for his opportunity after not playing as much as he would have liked to last year, and so is Rodney. Those two guys are really locked in."

When Stamps is not on the football field, he enjoys music. He plays the drums and the piano. His fascination with the drums goes back as long as he can remember. He picked up the piano when he got to high school.

Football is important, and so is his faith. His father, Albert Stamps, is a pastor. Ashton likes to play gospel songs and says that it provides a reprieve when he wants to think about something other than football or school.

"It's good to have something else to help keep me grounded," he says. "I've always liked music, and it helps me when I am having a hard time with something. As much as I love football, it's nice to have something else to get into."

title: Brent Venables names 'pound-for-pound' best athlete at Oklahoma
description: Brent Venables praises on Oklahoma standout as the team's best pound-for-pound athlete and a player with immense potential.
fullText:
The Oklahoma Sooners have some of the best athletes in college football. The Sooners are coming off a College Football Playoff berth and return several key contributors this upcoming season.

However, it's a player who hasn't played a ton up to this point in his career that head coach Brent Venables identified as the best athlete on the team. That player is EDGE rusher Danny Okoye. The former four-star prospect has totaled just six tackles, two tackles for loss and two sacks in his two seasons in Norman. He's competing with Adepoju Adebawore for a starting spot this year.

Venables was speaking to News 9's Toby Rowland, in which he called Okoye the best athlete on the team and said that he might have the potential to play football the longest at the professional level.

"Pound-for-pound, the best athlete on our team," Venables said via 'Oklahoma's Own.' "Incredibly explosive. Very hungry, driven. He's matured a lot. Just his lens and perspective. You're talking about a homeschooled guy that… has just been a piece of clay, and Danny probably has as much potential, maybe more than anybody, to play this game the longest."

The timing could be ideal for Okoye to emerge. Oklahoma enters 2026 with legitimate national championship aspirations and one of the deepest defenses in college football. If Okoye can win the starting job and translate his explosiveness into production, he could become another major weapon for Venables' defense.

More importantly, his development could give Oklahoma another high-level pass rusher as the Sooners prepare for another difficult SEC schedule. For a player Venables describes as the best athlete on the roster, 2026 could be the season Okoye finally shows why the coaching staff has been so high on him.

title: George Pickens and the Top 10 Cowboys playing in contract year in 2026
description: Contract years tend to bring out the best in players, as long as the team is in contention. Here's a look at the top Cowboys with a lot to play for.
fullText:
At the end of the day, this is a business. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones will never let anyone forget that plain fact, though he does bank on fanaticism blurring the lines in his favor far too often. Star NFL players have a passion for the game that allows them to put their bodies through the rigors of untold physical hardships. Often times the willingness to push their bodies 100% is the difference between being talented and being great.

But at the end of the day, the reward of millions of dollars is certainly a motivating factor. Each NFL player contributes to an NFL machine that creates billions in revenue, and rightly they want their fair share. With a collective bargaining agreement and a salary cap, the parameters are put in place for how much a player can earn, and their contracts determine when they are eligible to earn the most.

So contract years, the final season on a player's current deal, mean a ton. Players are either looking to convince heir current clubs to offer extensions, or they are auditioning for one of the other 31 clubs in free agency. That's the case for between 15-20 players on each team every season, and this year the Cowboys contingent is headlined by WR George Pickens.

Here's a look at the top Cowboys who are playing for their next big payday.

Anger is 38 and entering his 15th season. He hasn't been All-Pro worthy in a couple seasons, but he's more than serviceable and could extend his career in Dallas or elsewhere in 2027.

Miller is ring chasing at this point, but who knows how long the 37-year old will try to keep playing. A series of late-camp invites seem to be in his future as long as he can be a rotational contributor good for five sacks or more each season.

Patience is a virtue, and though he may still be WR6 for Dallas entering the season, Mingo has certainly turned the corner entering his fourth year in the league. That's if training camp and preseason are actually precursors. Mingo's biggest issue is that he may be bona fide, but may never see the field unless catastrophe strikes the league's top WR group.

Houston had 5.5 sacks last year and could be part of a much improved team effort in taking down the quarterback. Edge rushers get paid, even rotational ones, and having back-to-back years of health and production could be huge for his lifetime earnings.

Winters was a reserve he played a lot in SF after Fred Warner's injuries, but the 49ers traded him away. If he takes on a starter's role, mentality and leadership in his first season in Dallas, he certainly could earn an extension or a strong look on the open market come March.

Hooker took a pay cut to remain in Dallas, but Dallas didn't want to release him outright. Both speak volumes. Even if the Cowboys are done with him as a starter (now or after the year), he's rehabilitated his image as an injured player and should be able to latch on elsewhere in 2027.

Flournoy is a restricted free agent, but if he reaches the lofty goal of a 1,000-yard receiving season as the Cowboys' WR3, he'll earn a second-round tender at a minimum, if not a first. And that still might have other teams calling to submit an offer sheet.

Dallas seems to have high hopes on Durant elevating his play from what he was with the Rams now that he's in Christian Parker's system. If that comes to fruition, he could earn a solid contract in free agency this offseason.

Bass has a chance to not start a single game and still get paid; that's how good he's been in spot duty over the years, leading to being a second-round tender RFA this season. He can start for at least a dozen teams in the NFL right now.

Overshown's first mission is proving he can play an entire season's worth of games, something he hasn't done in three professional years. If he can do that, then his talent will take care of the rest as he's one of the most athletic linebackers in the league.

Pickens' situation is unique, as he's playing on the franchise tag and more than likely will be tagged again when the new league year comes around. He's absolutely auditioning for a long-term deal, whether in Dallas or in another city. He'll try to convince 31 other teams he's so good that he deserves top-of-the-market money AND trade compensation the Cowboys will rightfully demand if they don't extend him themselves.

title: Report: Jonathan Kuminga 'likes the idea of playing for the Lakers'

fullText:
With just over a month to go before NBA training camps open up, Jonathan Kuminga remains a free agent. The 23-year-old forward, who still has immense potential but has failed to realize much of it thus far, has been heavily linked to the Los Angeles Lakers all summer.

The Lakers were reportedly seriously interested in acquiring Kuminga earlier this summer, and perhaps they still have some interest in him. But he appears to be demanding an outsized contract, and it is unknown whether the Lakers have made any progress with the Atlanta Hawks on a potential sign-and-trade deal.

The Minnesota Timberwolves are the other main team interested in him. According to Kurt Helin of NBC Sports, Kuminga may prefer to head to the Purple and Gold.

"Kuminga reportedly likes the idea of playing for the Lakers — who would start him at the four — as a better fit."

But Helin also gave a reminder of the main issue Kuminga has had so far in his career.

"But is he? Kuminga wants to be a scorer, he's wanted the ball in his hands. In Los Angeles, where Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves have the ball, will he fit into the system and play a role? It's the same question in Minnesota. Before you say 'of course he will,' remember that clash was at the core of his issues with Steve Kerr in Golden State."

The narrative surrounding Kuminga is that he's been unwilling to sacrifice a reasonable amount of scoring and be a two-way player for a winning team. In his four and a half seasons with the Golden State Warriors, he was seen as a disappointment, and last season, he was benched by Kerr before getting traded to Atlanta.

If Los Angeles ends up landing Kuminga, it will be taking a pretty big risk. There is no indication, at least on the outside, that he has gotten to the point where he is truly ready to change his ways, but, of course, there is always the possibility that he will blossom very soon.

title: Arsenal star made guest of honour for former club’s derby match

Arsenal summer addition Christos Tzolis has made a strong first impression on Gunners supporters with some positive early performances, but the winger is seemingly just as popular with his former team Club Brugge.

Tzolis left Club Brugge for Arsenal in July, and it's not unusual for fans to turn on their best players in the aftermath of transfer exits. But that's certainly not the case here, as the 24-year-old was invited back as the guest of honour for the Bruges derby on Sunday.

Club Brugge hosted Cercle Brugge in the afternoon kick-off, and Tzolis was asked to take an honorary kick-off for the match.

Tzolis emerged from the tunnel to chants of "Tzolis! Tzolis! Tzolis!", with the player turning to applaud the home support. He then took the ceremonial kick-off before leaving the field with a huge smile on his face, greeting former teammates as he passed them.

With Arsenal last in action on Friday and a long gap to the next game on Monday, August 31st, Tzolis was free to make the quick trip across the English Channel to visit his old side.

But the Gunners will want the winger back in training this week, given he's been such an important part of the team's first two wins of the new season.

Tzolis provided two assists in Arsenal's Community Shield win over Manchester City, before playing an important role in the team's subsequent Premier League win over Coventry City.

It was only a deflection on his cross that denied Tzolis an official assist for Bukayo Saka's goal against Coventry, though as the player pointed out afterwards: "In the Fantasy [Premier League], it counts. I take the three points!"

The Giallorossi will look to bring in another winger to close out their summer window. Chelsea turned down their offer to sign Jamie Gittens on a loan with a €43M option to buy. The Blues paid €60M to add him last season and demand better terms. Malick Fofana lingers as an option, while PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye would be a younger and less established fallback.

He's not the most enticing name they tracked for the position, but he has excellent physical traits, is versatile, and his price tag better fits the role he's going to have compared to other deals they tried to set up.

title: The Red Sox – and Red Sox fans – have brought the magic back to Fenway Park
description: You can hear it from outside the building. That's how you know.
fullText:
Saturday night, the Red Sox were down 2-0 heading into the bottom of the ninth against the Giants. The crowd had been anxious all game—understandably—but something shifted when Caleb Durbin led off the inning with a walk. The noise inside a 114-year-old stadium started to rise and crescendoed in a walk-off that encapsulates the luck and magic of the 2026 Boston Red Sox.

The walk-off itself wasn't just something the crowd watched, though. It felt like something they willed into existence.

That's what's been happening at Fenway Park this summer. A building and a fanbase that has decided it's part of this team.

Sellouts, near-sellouts, 37,000-plus on a regular Friday night in August. You can cite the attendance figures, but the number that actually matters is decibels. Jerseys are coming off—the tarps-off phenomenon sweeping the bleachers, people yanking their shirts over their heads and spinning them in the air like rally towels. People in apartments on Boylston Street are posting videos of themselves hearing the roar from inside their living rooms. That's not a normal August at Fenway, or at least hasn't been for quite some time.

I was at last Monday's game against the Diamondbacks, and the crowd there had that same edge—that sense that nobody in the building was treating this as a casual summer night out. Even in a blowout, it's beyond apparent how engaged and just purely fun the stands at Fenway are right now. Yankees Suck chants breaking out unprompted, everyone screaming their heads off at Mr. Brightside during a pitching change, every single person leaping to their feet the moment Sweet Caroline came on. It was infectious. The energy is different this year. You can feel it the moment you walk through the gates.

Friday night was the purest version of it. Rafael Devers walked out for his first at-bat back at his old ballpark and Fenway didn't just boo—it rained boos on this man, 37,000 people making sure he knew exactly where he was and what this series meant. Whether you wanted boos or cheers, the crowd made its distain pretty well known, even to the chagrin of some other media pundits who were shocked there were so many jeers. Devers struck out. Later on, Willson Contreras hit one 450 feet over the Monster and the building became the loudest it's been all year.

This is what a pennant race sounds like.

After a stretch of Red Sox baseball where the question was whether anyone was going to bother showing up—the pandemic years, the "rebuilding years" with Chaim Bloom, the quiet Septembers, the half-filled sections and the general sense of waiting for something to happen—this summer has felt like a reset, not just in the standings, but in the relationship between this team and this city. For the years of apathy that permeated from ownership and the front office on down to Red Sox Nation, there's finally a well-earned feeling that everyone has bought in all at once.

The Red Sox are 25-11 since the All-Star Break, the best record in baseball over that stretch. They're back over .500 at home for the first time since April 17th. They have strong footing in the Wild Card hunt. And Fenway has responded the way Fenway responds when it actually believes in something—which is with everything it has, every night, from the first pitch to the ninth inning comeback.

The crowd needs the team to keep giving them reasons. The team needs the crowd in September. Right now, both sides of that deal are holding up their end. And it has been one of the most raucous, engaged, alive stretches this ballpark has seen in a very long time.

Go outside and stand on Lansdowne Street some time. You'll hear it.

title: NFL predictions: Previewing all 16 AFC teams & predicting every record in 2026
description: Division winners, win totals, playoff teams, and more!
fullText:
The 2026 NFL season is almost here, and the AFC looks loaded from top to bottom. Every division has at least one legitimate contender, while several teams could make the jump from afterthought to playoff team. Here is my division-by-division breakdown and prediction for all 16 AFC teams.

MORE: 5 most improved NFL offenses entering 2026-2027 season

Dec 21, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images

The Bills remain the safest bet in this division. Josh Allen is still the centerpiece, but the biggest change comes with Joe Brady taking over as head coach and Jim Leonhard running the defense. Buffalo also added DJ Moore to a receiving corps that desperately needed another difference-maker. The Bills won 12 games last season, and I expect them to remain near the top of the AFC. Prediction: 11-6, AFC East champions.

It's difficult to bet against the reigning AFC champions after what they accomplished last season. Drake Maye has another year of experience, and New England added A.J. Brown to an offense that already averaged 28.8 points per game in 2025. The Patriots will have enormous expectations, but I expect them to remain a serious contender. Prediction: 11-6, playoff team.

The Jets are better than the Dolphins, but that's not saying much. Geno Smith returns after leading the NFL in interceptions last season, while New York has completely reshaped its roster and enters 2026 with three first-round picks. There is enough talent here to surprise people, but the quarterback play has to improve dramatically. Prediction: 6-11.

Miami feels like a rebuilding team after moving on from Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill. Malik Willis now has an enormous opportunity, but expecting everything to click immediately is asking a lot. The Dolphins could be competitive in stretches, but this looks like the toughest roster in the division. Prediction: 5-12.

Dec 7, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) warms up before the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Casey-Imagn Images

The Ravens are my pick to bounce back after an ugly 8-9 season. John Harbaugh is gone, and Jesse Minter takes over, while Lamar Jackson gets a new offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle. Baltimore also added Trey Hendrickson and could get Nnamdi Madubuike back, potentially transforming a defense that struggled badly last year. Prediction: 11-6, AFC North champions.

Joe Burrow's health remains the biggest variable, but Cincinnati finally appears serious about fixing its defense. The Bengals added Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger before acquiring Dexter Lawrence. If Burrow stays healthy, this could be a dangerous team. Prediction: 10-7, playoff team.

The Steelers are fascinating because Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers could either make this look like a brilliant move or a desperate one. Pittsburgh also added Michael Pittman Jr., giving Rodgers another legitimate target. The defense has to improve, though, after ranking 26th in total defense last season. Prediction: 9-8.

The Browns are still rebuilding. Todd Monken takes over as head coach, the quarterback situation remains unsettled, and Cleveland traded Myles Garrett after his record-setting 2025 season. Jared Verse gives the defense a new centerpiece, but I don't expect the Browns to contend yet. Prediction: 5-12.

Division winner: Baltimore Ravens

MORE: 4 NFL players with most pressure entering 2026-2027 season

Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) throws during the first half of an AFC Wild Card Round game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images

The Texans are one of the most difficult teams to project. They went 12-5 last season and have an outstanding defense, but C.J. Stroud needs to rediscover his rookie form. Houston also completely revamped its offensive line and added David Montgomery to improve the running game. If the line finally stabilizes, the Texans could be a Super Bowl contender. Prediction: 11-6, AFC South champions.

Jacksonville won 13 games last season and remains one of the AFC's most intriguing teams. Travis Etienne is gone, leaving Bhayshul Tuten and others to replace his production, while Travis Hunter's two-way role will be fascinating to watch. If Brian Thomas Jr. takes a step forward, and Parker Washington continues his ascent, this offense could be dangerous. Prediction: 10-7, playoff team.

The Colts' entire season may depend on Daniel Jones staying healthy. Indianapolis saw its offense fall apart when Jones was injured last year, and the team is also dealing with major health questions involving Jonathan Taylor and DeForest Buckner. There's talent here, but too much uncertainty for me to trust them as a playoff team. Prediction: 8-9.

Everything revolves around Cam Ward. Tennessee brought in Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll to help develop its young quarterback and added veteran receiver Wan'Dale Robinson along with first-round pick Carnell Tate. I expect improvement, but the Titans are still a year away from seriously competing. Prediction: 6-11.

title: Annika Sorenstam's son talks smack toward Michigan at Barton Hills
description: Will McGee, 15, and Ava McGee, 16, were mic'd up during the U.S. Senior Open, and Will jokingly suggested a Michigan flag "be burned to the ground."
fullText:
ANN ARBOR — Annika Sorenstam never has been particularly known for her on-course smack talk.

But her kids, well, they're apparently not afraid to let it rip, especially when the cameras are watching them.

Mic'd up by the United States Golf Association for social-media content last week during the U.S. Senior Women's Open at Barton Hills Country Club in Ann Arbor, Will McGee, while following his famous mom around the course, spotted a maize-and-blue Michigan flag off in the distance, hanging in one of the hospitality tents.

"I hope they burn that Michigan flag down," Will McGee said. "That looks quite ugly."

"O-H-I-O," said Ava McGee, Will's sister.

Ava, 16, and Will, 15, live with Mom and Dad, Will McGee, in Florida, but it turns out, they have some allegiance to the state of Ohio. Father Mike McGee is from East Palestine, Ohio, and both Ava and Will were baptized there. East Palestine and Columbus aren't exactly close, about three hours from each other, but hey, Ohio is Ohio. So, there ya go.

Annika Sorenstam, 55, arguably the greatest women's golfer ever with 72 LPGA wins and 10 majors (despite retiring in her late 30s to start a family), finished runner-up at the U.S. Senior Women's Open. She held the lead twice, briefly, during Sunday's final round in her bid to win the championship for a second time (she won in 2021). Sorenstam finished the tournament at 4 under, two strokes back of champion and fellow Swede Maria McBride.

The week in Ann Arbor was a family affair. Mike McGee was on the bag at Barton Hills caddying for Sorenstam, who has finished top-10 in the U.S. Senior Women's Open all six times she has played in the tournament.

title: Mac McWilliams faces pivotal Eagles preseason finale
description: Mac McWilliams enjoyed some early momentum at camp, but injuries, missed opportunities and a crowded secondary may complicate his roster push.
fullText:
A month ago, Mac McWilliams looked like one of the easier roster projections on the Philadelphia Eagles' defense. The second-year cornerback wasn't generating the same headlines as Ty Robinson or Darius Cooper, but he was quietly doing what young players need to do to survive training camp and win a job.

He was stacking practices, earning opportunities, and giving coaches reasons to believe he could help down the road if called upon. Lately, however, the conversation has shifted, not because McWilliams has played poorly enough to eliminate himself from consideration. Rather, the circumstances around him have become increasingly complicated.

An old NFL saying. Availability is a skill, and being unavailable can be dangerous at this time of year. Just ask Johnny Wilson. After being waived with an injury designation and clearing waivers, he reverts to Philadelphia's injured reserve.

McWilliams can ball, but his most obvious concern right now is his health. He missed practice time recently with a groin injury before returning for Saturday night's preseason matchup against the New England Patriots. He then exited during the second quarter after appearing to sustain another injury and did not return.

For established veterans, a missed practice or preseason game isn't particularly meaningful. For guys on the back half of the depth chart who are fighting for roster spots, the story changes. Every missed rep carries weight. The Eagles are trying to make decisions with limited information. The fewer opportunities a player has to put positive tape on film, the harder it becomes to separate himself from the competition.

The larger issue may be simple roster math. Philadelphia's cornerback room is somewhat crowded. Jonathan Jones was added this offseason, but then again, he is also injured.

Riq Woolen isn't going anywhere. Kelee Ringo remains firmly in the mix. Jones is expected back from that shoulder injury at some point. The Eagles also continue evaluating young defensive backs while searching for answers at multiple spots in the secondary.

Meanwhile, players such as Shaun Wade continue creating splash plays. Wade has forced fumbles in consecutive preseason games,s making the coaching staff's decision-making more difficult.

Every strong performance elsewhere in the secondary creates another hurdle for McWilliams to clear. The preseason finale suddenly matters. This isn't a declaration that McWilliams won't make the roster, far from it. The Eagles invested a draft pick in him because they believe he possesses traits worth developing.

Those evaluations don't disappear after a couple of preseason games. Still, the margin for error feels smaller than it did a few weeks ago. The story of McWilliams' summer isn't that he has been overtaken by someone else. It's that injuries have interrupted his momentum at the exact moment other young defensive backs are gaining theirs.

That's what makes the preseason finale so important. Players like Ty Robinson and Darius Cooper have spent this entire camp forcing their way into roster conversations. McWilliams enters the final week needing an opportunity to remind everyone why he was already part of that discussion.

And if that opportunity doesn't come, the roster path that once appeared relatively straightforward could become much harder to navigate. If we were to wager, we'd bet on him making the team, but in professional football, one can never tell.

title: Robert Saleh: Offense has to be better
description: The Titans scored 10 points in the fourth quarter to end Sunday night's preseason game against the Seahawks with a win, but head coach Robert Saleh said the team's early performance left something to be desired in a postgame press conference.
fullText:
The Titans scored 10 points in the fourth quarter to end Sunday night's preseason game against the Seahawks with a win, but head coach Robert Saleh said the team's early performance left something to be desired in a postgame press conference.

Cam Ward started at quarterback for the second straight week and led the team to a field goal on their first drive, but failed to convert a fourth-and-1 on their second possession and fumbled on a sack to help set up a punt on his final series. Ward was 8-of-12 for 69 yards through the air before exiting the game.

All of that came against Seahawks backups and Saleh said that any of the good things that happened don't outweigh the need for the entire operation to improve.

"I thought the first drive was good, we went out there and got some points," Saleh said. "Thought Cam, again, was good with the ball, good decision-making. We just couldn't connect on a couple of deep throws, but, overall, it's got to be better. I'm not trying to sugarcoat it. It does got to be better, but at the same time, there's always going to be things that we can take from."

It's a bit better than Saleh's review of Ward's first preseason outing, but the Titans will need the progress to pick up for the offense to get where they want it to be for Week 1 against the Jets.

title: Barcelona condemn police action after supporter arrested before Elche clash
description: Barcelona’s 5-0 win over Elche was one of the biggest talking points of the opening weekend of the La Liga season, but an incident away from the pitch has now prompted a strong response from the clu...
fullText:
Barcelona's 5-0 win over Elche was one of the biggest talking points of the opening weekend of the La Liga season, but an incident away from the pitch has now prompted a strong response from the club.

Before kick-off, a Barcelona supporter was arrested by police following an incident involving an Estelada flag.

According to the club's account, security forces confiscated the flag before the supporter was struck several times and subsequently arrested.

FC Barcelona have now issued an official statement condemning what they described as the "disproportionate use of force against the club's members and supporters."

The club also offered support to the arrested young supporter and his family, while demanding clarity over an incident that has become a significant point of discussion.

The Barcelona supporter's arrest took place before the match against Elche, with the circumstances surrounding the incident now under scrutiny.

In their statement, Barça described the arrest as "disproportionate" and "inconsistent", making clear that the club is unhappy with how the situation was handled.

Barcelona also said they have offered their support to the supporter involved and his family should they require assistance.

"FC Barcelona has made itself available to the detained fan and his family to offer them any support they may require," read the official statement.

Furthermore, the Blaugrana made it clear that they are waiting for the relevant information from those involved before deciding whether any further steps are necessary.

Barcelona also used the statement to address another important part of the incident, which was the confiscation of Estelada flags from Barça supporters.

The club expressed regret that police officers had once again taken Estelada flags from supporters and stressed their view that the flag is a legal symbol.

"FC Barcelona also regrets that, once again, police officers confiscated Estelada flags from Barça fans.

"The Estelada is a legally endorsed symbol and its display constitutes a legitimate exercise of freedom of expression. As such, it cannot in itself be considered an incitement to hatred or violence.

"FC Barcelona is awaiting the relevant explanations regarding the events and reserves the right to take whatever action it deems appropriate to defend the integrity, rights and freedom of expression of its members and supporters, both at the Spotify Camp Nou and at rival teams' grounds," the statement concludes.

title: Who will step up to replace Koi Perich?
description: Kerry Brown leads the way at the safety position
fullText:
The Koi Perich era at Minnesota is over.

From the back-to-back game-ending interceptions against USC and UCLA in 2024 to the disastrous muffed punt against Cal in 2025, the Esko native's two-year tenure in the Twin Cities had its fair share of ups and downs.

However you felt about Perich — before or after his departure — only one thing matters now: He's gone.

So who is stepping up to replace him?

The good news is that safety has been a position of strength under head coach P.J. Fleck, with Antoine Winfield Jr., Jordan Howden, and Tyler Nubin all playing on Sundays.

And what many people outside of Minnesota don't seem to understand is that Perich was not the Gophers' top safety last year. That would be Kerry Brown, who finished fourth on the team with 56 total tackles, four tackles for loss, four pass break-ups, and two interceptions.

What a play by Kerry Brown! @GopherFootball 

📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/IbqLOFRC2I

Defensive coordinator and safeties coach Danny Collins covets versatility above all else, so you'll likely see Brown alternate between free safety, strong safety, and perhaps even some nickel throughout the season.

Next to Brown, fifth-year senior Aidan Gousby gives the Gophers a veteran option at safety. He flexed his own versatility last year when he started the last two games of the season at cornerback and acquitted himself well. The coaching staff seems content with what they have at cornerback for now, so Gousby has been spent fall camp taking snaps at strong safety and nickel, where he is competing with redshirt junior Garrison Monroe.

The Shakopee native has largely been a special teams contributor during his first three years with the program, and he missed nine games last season due to injury. Monroe was healthy for spring practice and seems well positioned to be a key contributor in the secondary this fall.

Here is what Fleck had to say about Monroe back in April:

"[Garrison Monroe] looks like a completely different player than he looked like in November, and that's strictly a credit to him, Coach Collins, and his dedication to film study. He's playing faster and way more confident. He's making a lot of plays."

The most talked about safety this fall has undoubtedly been sophomore Zack Harden.

You might remember Harden for posting "My Turn!!" on Twitter the same day the news broke that Perich had entered the transfer portal. He seems to be backing up that talk with his play in fall camp.

The coaching staff has been high on Harden since he arrived on campus last fall, when they made no attempt to preserve his redshirt, allowing him to see the field in 11 games, primarily on special teams.

He is another versatile option for Collins, taking snaps at free safety, strong safety, and nickel during camp. The physical tools are all there, but of course he lacks meaningful snaps at the collegiate level. Now it's a question of how soon he can get up to speed and limit the types of mistakes that come from inexperience.

Fleck was singing his praises after an open practice this fall:

"…I'm telling you, Zack Harden [is] one of the more under talked about players on our football team. Relentless, he's tough. He's [an] unbelievable teammate. He's passionate about football, loves football. He's a great student of the game."

"…He's relentless in the way he pursues. He is very very violent in the way he tackles. He can cover. He's long. So I'm looking forward to special things from him."

The other names to know are Lehigh transfer Mekhai Smith and Southwest Minnesota State transfer Parker Knutson. I don't see either of them starting this fall, but I believe both of them give the Gophers much needed depth at the position. Both could see snaps at safety or nickel.

Redshirt sophomore Zahir Rainer has been sidelined from fall camp with a leg injury and the timetable for his return is unknown, so I wouldn't expect to see him in uniform any time soon.

But expect to see a lot of Brown, Gousby, Monroe, and Harden when the Gopher defense takes the field.

title: Harry Wilson becomes Leeds United’s 900th senior player

Harry Wilson made history at the City Ground by becoming the 900th player to represent Leeds United in a senior competitive fixture.

The Wales international was named in Daniel Farke's starting line-up for the opening Premier League game of the 2026/27 campaign, helping the Whites secure a dramatic 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest.

Wilson joined Leeds on a free transfer during the summer after leaving Fulham and made his competitive debut alongside fellow new arrivals Tarik Muharemović (898) and James Trafford (899).

The landmark appearance came as Leeds began the new season with all three points, secured by Anton Stach's superb late free-kick.

Wilson is the latest player to claim a landmark place in the club's history, following Pierre-Michel Lasogga, who became the 800th player to represent Leeds in 2017.

Before him, Alex McCarthy reached the 700 mark, Seb Carole was the 600th and former England international Mark Hateley became number 500.

The earlier milestones belonged to Ian Baird at 400, Jim Storrie at 300, Jimmy Rudd at 200 and James Wilson, who became the club's 100th senior player.

The latest Wilson to wear the white shirt has now completed the journey to 900, marking the occasion with a winning debut on the banks of the River Trent.

title: The future of a Manchester City midfielder is now painstakingly clear

fullText:
If there was any further proof needed that Nico Gonzalez is surplus to requirements at Manchester City, it arrived yesterday. Fabrizio Romano reported last night that Newcastle United had made significant progress in their bid to sign Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City. Romano reports that the two clubs have almost agreed on a deal that will see the Spanish midfielder join Newcastle's rebuild. Furthermore, it is reported that Newcastle are in talks with Nico Gonzalez in a bid to seal the deal early this week.

Unfortunately, Nico Gonzalez has likely played his final game for Manchester City. He has spent 18 months at the club after signing for City from FC Porto in January 2025. During his time at the club, the Spanish midfielder showed signs that he could play an important role for the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. Nico could play as a defensive midfielder and he did step up in Rodri's absence last season. Looking at Enzo Maresca's current squad, it did seem like Nico Gonzalez could play that role this season.

But it isn't to be. For whatever reason, City have decided that it would be better to sell Nico Gonzalez. Perhaps the City hierarchy feel that the Spanish midfielder is a good midfielder, but not capable of reaching the level they desire. Perhaps Nico Gonzalez' isn't suited to playing in an Enzo Maresca side. Whatever their reasoning is, City seem poised to sell Nico to Newcastle.

Newcastle United are eager to sign Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City. After seeing Marc Guehi start ahead of fhe Spanish midfielder yesterday, a summer transfer may be exactly what Nico Gonzalez needs.

title: Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game over trans row
description: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom is ejected from the Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.
fullText:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday's Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Sitting at courtside, Kanter Freedom stood up with his arms outstretched and took steps towards the court after Cloud began pointing and shouting at him during a timeout.

Kanter Freedom was wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with the words "WOMAN noun. Adult human female.".

Earlier this month, he declared he would enter next season's WNBA Draft, citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.

Security and other Sky players intervened, before former Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics centre Kanter Freedom was escorted from the court.

He posted on X: "I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Writing on Threads after the game, Cloud said: "To every trans kid/person, you are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are & you will always be protected by me."

Kanter Freedom reportedly spoke with police officers before exiting Chicago's Wintrust Arena.

The Fever won the match 113-90.

"There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," said Sky head coach Tyler Marsh.

"That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too."

The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA

Sex toys again thrown on court during WNBA matches

On Saturday, the Sky's win over Golden State Valkyries was one of two WNBA matches interrupted after sex toys were thrown on to the court.

There were similar incidents last season when six WNBA matches in Atlanta, New York and Los Angeles were interrupted.

USA Today reported the same group responsible for last year's incidents has said it will continue to disrupt WNBA games to protest against the league's policy on transgender athletes.

The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.

On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

There are no transgender athletes currently competing in the league, but intense debate in the US has been sparked by recent comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham - who played in Sunday's match in Chicago - questioning the current rules.

description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said "execution" and "penalties" will be areas of emphasis going into final week of the preseason following loss to Bengals.
fullText:
There will be a lot of points of improvement for the Chicago Bears going into their last preseason game against the Tennessee Titans this Saturday after their rough loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

The Bengals game was a disaster for the Bears. There committed 11 penalties, multiple fumbles, although they never turned the ball over, only converted 2-of-14 third down attempts and failed to score a touchdown.  Quarterback Caleb Williams singled out execution and penalties as part of what Chicago focuses on next week as they prepare for the Titans.

"Execution, penalties, and just getting started," Williams said. "On the first play, we had a fumbled snap, so it's small things like that that add up.  It's just us being able to go out there and eliminate those mistakes. A lot of it comes down to focus, and that's something we can control."

Preseason games always need to be taken with a grain of salt given the first string only played one drive. However, the starters were not immune to these problems as the Bears had a penalty on their opening drive that stalled them in the red zone. This was a problem at times last season as well.

Chicago has enough time before their regular season opener against the Carolina Panthers on Sept. 13 to address some of these issues. The Bears cannot afford to have these types of struggles in the regular season as the NFC North is expected to be a competitive division between the Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and even the Minnesota Vikings with Kyler Murray at quarterback.

fullText:
Developers who met through Australia’s improv scene and publishers of comedic party games have united for this slithering challenge in which you play as one extended limb

Most stealth games cast you as a spy, an assassin or a master thief. My Arms Are Longer Now dispenses with most of the criminal person, to send in just one spectacularly badly behaved limb. It slithers across floors, winds around furniture, steals things and slaps anyone within reach – finally answering the question nobody asked: what if your own arm turned to crime?

As Toot Games co-founder Matthew Jackson puts it: “You are the bad thing that happens to the people.”

The idea began as a much simpler prototype made during a weekend game jam themed around the idea of lost and found. Jackson and fellow Toot co-founder Millie Holten, who met through Melbourne’s improv and sketch comedy community, wanted an idea that could be understood – and raise a laugh – in a single still image. A grotesquely extended arm proved to be just that.

Since then, the game has been all about comedy. It has more than 40 speaking characters, voiced by Australian comedians who perform the written dialogue before improvising alternative takes. “It’s a vessel for jokes,” Jackson says. For almost a year, development largely involved trying to “cram jokes into the game”; only later did the team realise the physics of the increasingly sophisticated arm had become fun in their own right. Players can personalise its skin tone, hair and accessories, making it less somebody else’s disembodied crime spree than a freaky extension of their own body.

The stealth here owes something to Untitled Goose Game: characters react to your crimes, but, Jackson says, “There are no fail states in the game.” A museum guard might smack the arm, or beg it to stop before they are fired. Anyone can be slapped, including an infant. While searching for a publisher, Jackson repeatedly asked: “Is someone going to come and tell us you can’t slap the baby?” Jackbox Games, thankfully, did not.

Making that slap possible required rather more sophistication than the joke might suggest. The original game was flat and 2D, but Holten’s concept art showed the arm looping over tables, under chairs and around objects. Six months into development, the studio took the risky decision to rebuild in 3D. Working with developer Cherie Davidson, Jackson created a procedural, tube-like limb and a system that uses forced perspective to preserve the illustrated style while allowing the physical collisions the game needs.

The work never quite ends. The team calls another session tinkering with the troublesome appendage “going into the armpit”.

That labour is particularly demanding because comedy is finite. “You can hit a joke, and that joke’s done. You’ve burnt that,” Jackson says. Some publishers suggested adding more puzzles, but Toot feared they would obstruct the punchlines. Jackbox understood that it was meant to be “a good time, not a long time”, with players who do poke into every corner rewarded with optional interactions and voice lines.

Jackson’s ultimate ambition for the game is appropriately simple: “I hope players say it was funny. That’s truly it.” And after three years in the armpit, 48 speaking characters, and one non-negotiable baby slap, Toot Games has gone to extraordinary lengths to reach gaming’s funny bone.
